title: Universal Drag Handles and Drop Zone Highlighting
description: Add a consistent drag-handle affordance (grip-vertical icon) to every draggable UI element in ui/js/react/index.tsx, and highlight all valid drop zones (passively) while a compatible drag is in flight, keeping the existing stronger indicator on the currently hovered target. Handle-only drag initiation on select-first elements (panel tabs, mode/window tabs, reorderable tree rows); whole-surface drag retained on drag-first elements (tree-unit headers, catalogue/palette items, mode tab-gap stack drag, DraggableAvatar). Handles always visible (muted, brighten on hover). Plan approved at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-everything-that-is-silly-wolf.md.
summary:
Follow-up styling fixes addressing three reported inconsistencies in ui/js/react/index.tsx:

1. **Preview/ready state must emphasize labels+icons like active does.** Root cause: icon and label spans across the tree (`renderTreeRowIcon`, `TreeSection`'s label span) hardcoded their own `text-element` color, which as an explicit child declaration always wins over an ancestor's inherited `text-emphasized` — so the passive drop-zone-ready state (and, latent but real, the pre-existing selected/highlighted states) never actually emphasized icons, only whatever inherited by accident. Fixed by giving `renderTreeRowIcon` an `emphasized` parameter (and stripping the redundant hardcoded color from the default-icon class so it purely inherits), and threading a computed `rowEmphasized = isSelected || isHighlighted || isDropReady` (or `isDropReady` alone for sections) into every icon/label render across `TreeItem`, `SortableTreeItem`, and `TreeSection`.

2. **Active elements must also emphasize their own drag handle.** `DragHandle` hardcoded `text-muted-foreground` regardless of context. Added an `emphasized` prop (falls back to muted, matches ambient `text-emphasized` when true) and wired it at every call site from the state that already drives that element's own label emphasis: panel tabs (`isActive && showActiveColor` or leaf-tab tree-unit drop-readiness), tree rows (`rowEmphasized`), panel tree-unit headers (`unitDragActive`), and mode/window tabs (a newly computed per-tab `tabActive`).

3. **Hovering the drag handle must only highlight the handle, not the whole element.** Root cause: plain CSS `:hover` on a container is true whenever the pointer is anywhere in its box, including over a nested drag handle — there's no way to "stop" that in CSS aside from excluding it structurally. Added two small helpers, `selfHoverExcludingHandle`/`groupHoverExcludingHandle`, which wrap a hover utility in a `:not(:has([data-slot='drag-handle']:hover))` guard (a no-op wherever no drag handle exists, so safe to apply unconditionally). Applied to every hover-reactive class that can contain a drag handle: `interactiveActiveFillClass` (covers panel tabs' and mode tabs' active-state hover, since both alias it), `panelTabButtonClass`, `modeDockTabClassName`, and the tree row shell/content-fill hover branches (`treeRowChromeShellClasses`, `treeRowChromeContentFillClasses`).

Also restored the panel tree-unit header's drag handle, which a concurrent session had removed while this ticket was in progress (closing ticket REMOVE-PANEL-TREE-DRAG-ICONS, issue #2000) — per explicit instruction, re-added using the same consistent trailing-`DragHandle` pattern (not the old leading-icon placement that motivated that removal), restored the `unit.label || draggable` header-visibility condition so undraggable-looking unlabeled units still surface their handle, and applied the same emphasis/fill-vs-text-color fixes there.

Along the way, fixed same-element conflicting-text-color-class risks (a base muted/element color class co-present with an added emphasized/accent class relies on Tailwind's internal generation order rather than deterministic override) by switching to single conditional (ternary) text-color selection in `PanelTreeUnitsPane`'s header and `PanelEmptyDockZone`, and by fixing the tree drop-zone fill to apply only to the same content-column area the existing selected/highlighted states already paint (not the outer shell, which would bleed into the guide gutter or, for expandable property rows, into nested content).

Verification: typecheck (75 pre-existing unrelated errors, zero referencing any new/changed symbol — same baseline pattern as prior rounds), lint (same single pre-existing unrelated rule-definition error), the `check-no-raw-colors` guardrail (zero violations in index.tsx), and the test suite (257 passed / 14 pre-existing unrelated failures, identical set to the prior baseline) all show no regressions. Browser-based visual verification was still not attempted this round given the tooling was unresponsive in the prior session; recommend visually confirming hover isolation and emphasis in a working browser session, since `:has()`-based selector exclusion is inherently harder to verify statically than via typecheck/lint/tests.
